test_title: PYST 20: SSC CGL - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On : 21 April 2022 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 52° and ∠ABD = 47°. What is the difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
solution:
**Given:**

∠CAB = 52° and ∠ABD = 47°

**Concept used:**

The angle subtended by the diameter at any point on the circumference is equal to 90°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9fbfeea21bd1cb1f145ad930e85feae1d41e56c2c28d0c31d246ede66a506fcf.png] 

According to the concept,

∠ACB = ∠ADB = 90°

So, ∠CBA = 180° - (90° + 52°)

⇒ 180° - 142°

⇒ 38°

Similarly,

∠BAD = 180° - (90° + 47°)

⇒ 180° - 137°

⇒ 43°

So, ∠CAD = 52° + 43°

⇒ 95°

∠CBD = 38° + 47°

⇒ 85°

Now,

∠CAD - ∠CBD = 95° - 85°

⇒ 10°

**∴ The difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD is 10.**
